comparison: Both address claims C124-C126 about broader applicability of the mechanism. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the applicability to other systems remains speculative without additional evidence. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, emphasizing the fundamental theoretical contributions and general applicability based on first principles. Disagreement on whether broader claims are sufficiently supported.

Both address claims C127-C129 about alternative mechanisms. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, praising appropriate acknowledgment of other mechanisms. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 1 identifying as a weakness the lack of quantification of which mechanism is predominant and absence of analysis of crosstalk between mechanisms. Disagreement on whether alternative mechanisms are adequately addressed.

Both address claims C113-C121 about proposed experimental tests. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes predictions logically follow from the model and are well-reasoned and testable. Peer review explicitly praises this as a major strength that will inspire new experimental techniques. Strong agreement.

Both address claims C9, C42-C44, C108-C109 about experimental validation. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes quantitative agreement with experimental data using only one fitting parameter. Peer review affirms validation across all three reviewers with no concerns raised. Strong agreement.

Both address claims C8, C39 about IDR enhancement of binding affinity and search speed. OpenEval also includes C62 on energy-entropy trade-off. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval cites equilibrium analysis and dynamical simulations. Peer review notes all three reviewers affirm with 'compelling evidence' and 'rigorous' derivations. Strong agreement.

Both address claims C45-C47 about modeling assumptions. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, noting assumptions are reasonable and appropriately justified. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, with Reviewer 3 questioning how ubiquitous the assumed DNA binding site architecture is among eukaryotic TFs. Disagreement on whether key structural assumptions reflect biological reality.

Both address claims C74, C76 about distinction from bacterial facilitated diffusion. Peer review also includes C34-C35 on FD limitations in eukaryotes. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes valid comparison grounded in established knowledge. Peer review indicates all reviewers accept this distinction, emphasizing novelty for eukaryotes. Strong agreement.

Both address claims about the single-round 3D-1D search mechanism (C40, C72-C73, C77). Peer review also includes octopusing mechanism claims (C78-C79, C103, C105-C107). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes simulation data and analytical calculations. Peer review calls it 'elegant' and 'fundamental contribution' with all reviewers supporting. Strong agreement on core mechanism.

OpenEval R12 addresses octopusing mechanism (C78-C79, C103) while peer R2 covers broader set including single-round search and octopusing. Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes mechanism observed in simulations and represents novel insight. Peer review praises as 'elegant resolution' with 'interesting biological implications.' Strong agreement.

OpenEval emphasizes compensatory dynamics achieving both high diffusion and low detachment. Peer review praises mechanism for accommodating stability and 1D diffusion simultaneously. Strong agreement on this aspect.
